what: The rule catalogue of the explainable diagnosis (configs/schemas/diagnosis.schema.json, docs/diagnosis.md). Every rule_id an agent emits must be here. One name per cause on every platform: a missing executable is svc.image_missing on Windows (7000 / error 2) and on Linux (status=203/EXEC). `certainty` is the highest certainty the rule may give; `proven_when` / `likely_when` say on which evidence. Rules are evaluated in `order`; the first matching rule is the leading finding, later matches are listed after it.

svc.not_installed.title: There is no such service on this host

proven_when.linux: LoadState=not-found — no unit file defines it

svc.disabled.title: The service is blocked from starting by its configuration

proven_when.windows: start type is Disabled (QueryServiceConfig dwStartType=4), or the start failed with error 1058
proven_when.linux: the unit is masked (LoadState=masked or UnitFileState=masked)

svc.image_missing.title: The program the service runs does not exist

proven_when.windows: the image file of ImagePath does not exist, or event 7000 carries error 2 (file not found) or 3 (path not found)
proven_when.linux: ExecMainStatus=203 (EXEC) and the ExecStart path does not exist

likely_when.linux: ExecMainStatus=203 and the path exists (not executable, wrong interpreter)

svc.image_path_unquoted.title: The image path contains a space and is not quoted

likely_when.windows: ImagePath has a space before the executable name and no quotes — Windows may try a shorter path first

svc.blocked_by_policy.title: An application-control policy blocked the service's program

proven_when.windows: an enforcement block event names the image — AppLocker 8004 ("EXE and DLL") or Code Integrity / WDAC 3077 (plan B14); the image's Authenticode trust (WinVerifyTrust) is attached as context, since unsigned or untrusted is the usual cause

svc.account_missing.title: The account the service runs as does not exist

proven_when.windows: the service account (lpServiceStartName) cannot be resolved to a SID, or event 7038 with error 1332
proven_when.linux: ExecMainStatus=217 (USER), or User= names no account

svc.logon_failed.title: The service account could not log on

proven_when.windows: event 7038 with its LogonUser error (disabled, locked out, password expired, wrong password), or error 1069 together with the account state that explains it

likely_when.windows: error 1069 (status or newest event 7000) with no event naming the reason

svc.logon_right_missing.title: The service account lacks the right to log on as a service

proven_when.windows: event 7041 (the account was not granted the logon type), a 7038 with error 1385, or LSA shows neither the account nor one of its groups holding SeServiceLogonRight / a SeDenyServiceLogonRight

svc.access_denied.title: The service account may not read or execute what it needs

proven_when.windows: AuthzAccessCheck of the service account's SID on the image or its folder denies FILE_EXECUTE / FILE_READ_DATA — the denying or missing ACE named
proven_when.linux: ExecMainStatus=243 (CREDENTIALS) / 238 (STATE_DIRECTORY), or the journal shows EACCES on a path the unit owns

likely_when.linux: the journal reports 'Permission denied' on /var/lib, /var/cache or /var/log

svc.dependency_failed.title: A service it depends on did not start

proven_when.windows: event 7001/7003 for the service, or a dependency (direct, via a load-order group, recursively) is not running — the finding points at the FIRST failed link
proven_when.linux: Result=dependency, or a Requires=/BindsTo= unit is failed — recursively, first failed link

svc.dependency_failed.remedy_note: the remedy repairs the first failed link (its own cause), or removes the dependency

svc.deadlock.title: The service's threads wait on each other — a deadlock

proven_when.windows: Wait Chain Traversal (GetThreadWaitChain) reports a cycle for a thread of the service's process: each lock or thread in the chain is owned by the next, back to the first (plan B14)

svc.timeout.title: The service did not report as started in time

proven_when.windows: event 7009 or 7011, or error 1053 (in the status or in the newest event 7000 — the status resets to 0 after a failed start); with an Application 1000 crash of the image in the window it is reported as svc.crash instead
event 7031/7034 together with an Application 1000/1026 for the service's image

likely_when.windows: event 7031/7034 without a matching application error

svc.oom_killed.title: The kernel killed the service for lack of memory

svc.start_limit.title: systemd stopped retrying after too many failed starts

proven_when.linux: Result=start-limit-hit, or systemd's own journal message 'Start request repeated too quickly' (systemd 257 keeps Result=exit-code)

svc.condition_failed.title: A start condition of the unit is not met

proven_when.linux: ConditionResult=no with a ConditionTimestamp (evaluated), or AssertResult=no with an AssertTimestamp — a unit that never ran reports ConditionResult=no without a timestamp; or systemd's own journal message that the unit was skipped because of an unmet condition (a skipped unit is garbage-collected and its properties reset)

svc.exits_immediately.title: The service starts and exits at once with an error code

proven_when.windows: event 7023/7024 (service-specific error) or 7034, with the exit code from QueryServiceStatusEx
proven_when.linux: Result=exit-code with ExecMainStatus not 0 and not a systemd status (200-243)

likely_when.linux: the invocation's journal shows a configuration parse error (unknown directive, error parsing … at line N, invalid option)

svc.config_incomplete.title: The configuration lacks values the site must supply

likely_when.linux: the journal reports a value that is not configured (not specified, please define, no configuration found, missing option) — the shipped file is a template that needs site values

svc.peer_unreachable.title: The program cannot reach a service it needs

likely_when.linux: the journal shows connection refused / cannot connect to a database or peer

svc.network_unavailable.title: The program cannot resolve or reach the network

likely_when.linux: the journal shows name resolution failures

svc.not_initialized.title: The program needs a one-time initialisation first

likely_when.linux: the journal asks for an init step (e.g. --initdb, database not initialized)

svc.device_missing.title: A device the program needs is not present

likely_when.linux: the journal reports no such device / missing hardware

svc.container_limit.title: The environment does not allow what the program needs

likely_when.linux: the journal shows 'Operation not permitted' for kernel features, or a ConditionVirtualization excluding containers

svc.stopped_cleanly.title: The service is stopped and its last run ended without error

proven_when.windows: the service is stopped with Win32ExitCode 0 and a Service Control Manager stop recorded (7036/7040), or start type Manual and never started since boot
proven_when.linux: the unit is inactive with Result=success — stopped cleanly, never started, or a oneshot that ran and finished

svc.recent_incident.title: The service hit a recent incident before now — it crashed, exited abnormally, or threw

likely_when.windows: the agent's ETW incident ring holds a recent event for the service's image or last pid — a process exit with a non-zero code, an image crash, or a .NET exception (plan docs/etw-ringbuffer-plan.md); it describes a PAST invocation, so never above Likely
likely_when.linux: the agent's incident ring (fed by the eBPF collector) holds a recent event for the service's cgroup or last pid — an OOM kill or a fatal signal; a PAST invocation, so never above Likely

svc.unexplained.title: The target is not running and no rule explains why

unknown_when.windows: no rule matched; the finding cites the state and the events that were read, and names what was not observable
unknown_when.linux: no rule matched; the finding cites the unit state and the journal that was read

upd.up_to_date.title: The host has no pending updates

proven_when.windows: windows_update_facts reports zero pending updates and the last search succeeded
proven_when.linux: the package manager reports nothing upgradable

upd.behind.title: The host is behind on updates

proven_when.windows: windows_update_facts lists pending updates, with the security/critical count among them
proven_when.linux: the package manager lists upgradable packages, with the count from the security suite among them

upd.reboot_pending.title: A reboot is pending and blocks further updates

proven_when.windows: a reboot is pending (Component Based Servicing RebootPending or WindowsUpdate RebootRequired)
the newest update history entry has ResultCode Failed with its HResult, named in Windows' own words
proven_when.linux: the package manager or dpkg reported an error on the last run

upd.wsus_unreachable.title: The assigned WSUS server did not answer

likely_when.windows: a policy assigns a WSUS (UseWUServer=1, WUServer set) but the last search did not succeed

likely_when.linux: the package manager could not reach a configured repository on the last update

proven_when.linux: packages are held (apt-mark hold / dpkg hold / dnf versionlock) or phased and not yet offered, each named with the reason

upd.dpkg_interrupted.title: A previous package operation was interrupted

proven_when.linux: dpkg is in an interrupted state and needs `dpkg --configure -a`

upd.unexplained.title: The host's update state could not be explained

unknown_when.windows: no rule matched; the finding cites what windows_update_facts returned and names what was not measurable
unknown_when.linux: no rule matched; the finding cites what the package manager returned and names what was not measurable
